concepts.proposed_markdown: A worked hybrid model combines a recurring per-seat subscription with pooled monthly credits that fund several usage products. The included credits expire each month, while an optional prepaid top-up can remain available for a longer access period. Metronome links the recurring grant to the subscription so quantity changes can adjust credit provisioning under configured proration; balance and spend alerts remain merchant action signals rather than automatic access enforcement.
warnings: Keep the prices, credit quantities, products, expiration periods, and thresholds scoped to the fictional SeatsCo example.
The explicit `subscription_config` payload configures prorated seat increases; do not infer the exact seat-decrease calculation from this guide alone.
Do not describe threshold or spend alerts as native entitlement enforcement.

concepts.proposed_markdown: - [[source-metronome-guides-pricing-packaging-billing-model-guides-hybrid-business-models]] — worked hybrid subscription, pooled recurring credits, top-ups, and merchant-owned usage controls

A recurring credit or commit can be linked to a subscription so subscription quantity changes automatically provision and track credit according to configured proration. The hybrid-model example uses a pooled monthly recurring credit and explicitly sets `apply_seat_increase_config.is_prorated: true` for mid-month seat additions. Although the guide's prose also covers quantity decreases, it does not show a separate seat-decrease configuration or calculation rule.
warnings: Do not generalize the fictional plan's 100-credit monthly grant or expiry to all subscriptions.
Keep the seat-decrease behavior uncertain beyond the guide's high-level prose; only seat-increase proration is explicit in the shown configuration.
